There is a theory that it is the founder of {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine|ja|住吉神社|qid=Q11381857}} located all over the country, and it is also considered one of the ``three great Sumiyoshi'' along with {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|de|Sumiyoshi-Taisha|es|Sumiyoshi Taisha|fa|سومییوشی-تایشا|fi|Sumiyoshi-taisha|fr|Sumiyoshi-taisha|it|Grande santuario di Sumiyoshi|ja|住吉大社|ko|스미요시 대사|la|Sumiyoshi-taisha|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနန်းကွန်းနန်းရင်း|pt|Sumiyoshi taisha|ru|Сумиёси-тайся|sl|Veliko svetišče Sumijoši-taiša|th|ศาลเจ้าซูมิโยชิ|tr|Sumiyoshi-taisha|uk|Сумійосі тайся|zh|住吉大社|qid=Q705949}} in Osaka and {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|ja|住吉神社 (下関市)|simple|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|zh|住吉神社 (下關市)|qid=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} in Shimonoseki.<ref>{{Cite book |Japanese book |editor=Mutsuhiko Mori |title=Number Dictionary |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing |year=1987 |page=135}}</ref>.This is a shrine dedicated to {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013}}, the guardian deities of navigation. == Enshrined God ==
The following five deities are enshrined. </ref>. These five pillars are also collectively known as ``Sumiyoshi Gosho Okami.''

(Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|Sumiyoshi Shrine}}, compared to {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|de|Sumiyoshi-Taisha|es|Sumiyoshi Taisha|fa|سومییوشی-تایشا|fi|Sumiyoshi-taisha|fr|Sumiyoshi-taisha|it|Grande santuario di Sumiyoshi|ja|住吉大社|ko|스미요시 대사|la|Sumiyoshi-taisha|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနန်းကွန်းနန်းရင်း|pt|Sumiyoshi taisha|ru|Сумиёси-тайся|sl|Veliko svetišče Sumijoši-taiša|th|ศาลเจ้าซูมิโยชิ|tr|Sumiyoshi-taisha|uk|Сумійосі тайся|zh|住吉大社|qid=Q705949}} in Osaka) {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.On the other hand, in our company's origin story, we attribute this to Awagihara, where the Sumiyoshi deity was born. }}{{Refnest|group=Notes|Approximately 10 kilometers west of Sumiyoshi Shrine is Hyuga Pass, and approximately 10 kilometers northeast is Aoyagi (Awagi?), Koga City. It is also associated with place names such as Mt. Tachibana (Tachibana?) and the foothills of Mt. Bito (Odo?) to the north. }}. Among these theories, "Nihonshoki" <ref group="Hara"> "Nihonshoki" includes an article dated September 10, 9th year, 9th year of Emperor Chuai's reign, in the pre-Regency period of Empress Jingu. In </ref>, an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{ill|Yosami no Otarumi|ja|依網男垂見|qid=Q24899491|lt=Yorami Agohiko Tarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}.

There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage.

Shrines in each of them, so there is a theory that these shrines, including ours, had the intention of locating them at key points on the Korean route {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. In this, Sumiyoshi was considered to be the national guardian deity of navigation because it was inseparable from the conquest tradition of Empress Jingu, and the {{jalink|Five Kings of Wa|Q There is also a theory that he was deeply involved in the military and diplomacy of {{ill|Yamato Kingship|eo|Jamato (regno)|es|Reinado de Yamato|fa|پادشاهی یاماتو|fi|Yamato (valtio)|fr|Royauté de Yamato|ja|ヤマト王権|ko|야마토 정권|ru|Ямато (государство)|sr|Јамато (држава)|uk|Ямато (держава)|vi|Vương quyền Yamato|zh|大和王权|qid=Q2658252}} from around 1152880}} {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}.

The shrine's territory appears to be ``Sumiyoshi-sho'' in literature, and its affiliation continued through changes such as Goshirakawa-inryo, Senyomon-inryo, Fushimi-inryo, and Imperial family territory {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}.

Orie Yokota, the chief priest of the {{ill|Tenpō|de|Tempō|eo|Tenpo-epoko|fa|تنپو|fr|Ère Tenpō|ja|天保|ko|덴포|pl|Tenpō|pt|Tenpō|ru|Тэмпо|simple|Tenpō|sr|Тенпо|sv|Tenpō|tr|Tenpō|zh|天保 (日本)|qid=Q1369045}} era, revived Shinto rituals that had been forbidden by the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|es|Dominio de Fukuoka|fa|قلمرو فوکوئوکا|fr|Domaine de Fukuoka|ja|福岡藩|ko|후쿠오카번|pt|Domínio de Fukuoka|ru|Фукуока (княжество)|uk|Фукуока-хан|zh|福岡藩|qid=Q208766}}. Wish, {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|az|Hakozaki məbədi|cy|Creirfa Hakozaki|de|Hakozaki-gū|eu|Hakozaki santutegia|fr|Hakozaki-gū|ja|筥崎宮|tr|Hakozaki Tapınağı|zh|筥崎宮|qid=Q714742}} and the chief priests of {{ill|Umi Hachiman-gū|fr|Umi Hachiman-gū|ja|宇美八幡宮|th|ศาลเจ้าอูมิฮาจิมัง|qid=Q924940}} and {{jalink|Kyoto|Q740 When he complained to the {{ill|Ichijō family|ca|Família Ichijō|de|Ichijō (Familie)|fa|خاندان ایچیجو|fr|Famille Ichijō|it|Clan Ichijō|ja|一条家|ko|이치조가|pt|Família Ichijō|ru|Итидзё (род)|zh|一条家|qid=Q1535498}} of 246}}, he was arrested and ordered to return home by the domain, and in 1833, he retired and {{ja link|Zashiki prison|Q11486150}}<ref>The Life of Chobei Omiwa, Yasukuni Ashitsu (Ashitsu Office, 2008) p42</ref>.

== Precincts ==
[[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (Important cultural property)}}{{small|The style of the shrine building is "Sumiyoshi-zukuri". }}]]
The area of the precincts is 8,107 tsubo (2.68 hectares) <ref name="Yoshisho"/>. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area around the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River.Among the shrine buildings in the precincts, the {{ill|Shinto architecture|ar|عمارة الشنتو|de|Japanische Schreinarchitektur|fr|Architecture shinto|he|אדריכלות השינטו|hu|Sintó építészet|id|Arsitektur jinja|it|Architettura shintoista|ja|神社建築|ru|Синтоистская архитектура|simple|Shinto architecture|sl|Šintoistična arhitektura|zh|神社建築|qid=Q3080012|lt='''main shrine'''}} was built in the early {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Έντο|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|new|इदो काल|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} period. It is {{ill|Kirizuma-style|zh|悬山顶|qid=Q13308575}} with 4 girders (depth) and 2 beams (frontage), and the roof is {{ill|cypress bark roof|ja|檜皮葺|zh|檜皮葺|qid=Q90373477}}. The straight lines of the roof and the three {{ill|Bargeboard|af|Windveer|de|Ortgang|es|Tapacán|fr|Rive de toit|ja|破風|mr|बार्जबोर्ड|nn|Vindskie|no|Vindskie|si|වඩිම්බුව|sv|Vindskida|zh|博风板|qid=Q4881511}} and {{ill|chigi and katsuogi|ja|千木・鰹木|qid=Q87220234|lt=chigi/kataogi}} reflect the ancient architecture. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. <ref name="Kuni Honden"/><ref>[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t6&fields=f767&id=1307-4&bunrui=kuni_yuke_kenz_juyo Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). </ref><ref name="fukuokacityhonden">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/140 Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties Protection Division ``Fukuoka City Cultural Properties''). </ref><ref name="historical book"/>.The {{ill|Shinto architecture|ar|عمارة الشنتو|de|Japanische Schreinarchitektur|fr|Architecture shinto|he|אדריכלות השינטו|hu|Sintó építészet|id|Arsitektur jinja|it|Architettura shintoista|ja|神社建築|ru|Синтоистская архитектура|simple|Shinto architecture|sl|Šintoistična arhitektura|zh|神社建築|qid=Q3080012|lt='''haiden'''}} built in front of the main shrine is {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}} and has a copper plate roof. This Noh theater hall is a modern Japanese-style building that combines traditional Japanese and Western styles, and has been designated as a designated cultural property by Fukuoka City. </ref><ref name="Explanation board">Precinct information board. </ref>.

In addition, there are shrine buildings such as a Kagura hall and a Shinto gate within the precincts.

== Sessha ==
There are a total of 8 Setsusha shrines, 2 Setsusha shrines and 6 Setsusha shrines<ref name="Yoshisho"/>.

== Sessha ==
[[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Shiga-jinja and Funarama-jinja.JPG|thumb|230px|right|{{center|Funatama Shrine (right) and Shiga Shrine (left)}}]]
* Funatama Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|az|Sarutahiko|fa|ساروتاهیکو اوکامی|fr|Sarutahiko Ōkami|it|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|ko|사루타히코 오카미|mni|ꯁꯔꯨꯇꯍꯤꯀꯣ ꯑꯣꯀꯃꯤ|pl|Sarutahiko|ru|Сарутахико|simple|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ta|சருதாகிகோ அகாமி|tr|Sarutahiko Ōkami|zh|猿田彥|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: September 9th.
* Shiga Shrine - Enshrined Deity: {{ill|Watatsumi|abstract|Q1474187|az|Vatatsumi|de|Watatsumi|es|Watatsumi|fa|واتاتسومی|fr|Watatsumi|hu|Vatacumi|ja|ワタツミ|ko|와타쓰미|mni|ꯋꯇꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|pl|Watatsumi|ru|Ватацуми|simple|Watatsumi|uk|Вататсумі|zh|綿津見|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi Three Gods}}. Regular festival: June 1st.

== Main festivals ==
;Oiina Festival
: "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held <ref name="Winter">[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website)</ref><ref name="Historical Record"/>.
; Oda Festival
: "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest.
; Shiohi Festival
: "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land.
; Nagoshi Grand Festival
: “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities.
; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|Yabusame|ar|يابوسامه|az|Yabusame|da|Yabusame|de|Yabusame|es|Yabusame|fa|یابوسامه|fr|Yabusame|it|Yabusame|ja|流鏑馬|ko|야부사메|pl|Yabusame|ru|Ябусамэ|simple|Yabusame|sv|Yabusame|tr|Yabusame|uk|Ябусаме|zh|流鏑馬|zh_classical|流鏑馬|qid=Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered.
; Shooting Festival
: "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|de|Dazaifu (Amt)|fa|دازایفو (دولت)|fr|Dazaifu (gouvernement)|ja|大宰府|ko|다자이후|nl|Dazaifu (gebied)|pt|Dazaifu (governo)|ru|Дадзайфу (учреждение)|tg|Дазаифу|uk|Дадзайфу|zh|大宰府|qid=Q144845}} official who, during the {{ill|Emperor Yōzei|ar|الإمبراطور يوزيه|azb|یوزی (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Yōzei Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر یۆزێی|cs|Józei|cy|Yozei, ymerawdwr Japan|de|Yōzei|el|Αυτοκράτορας Γιόζεϊ|es|Yōzei Tennō|fa|امپراتور یوزی|fr|Yōzei|id|Yōzei|it|Yōzei|ja|陽成天皇|ko|요제이 천황|nl|Yozei|pl|Yōzei|pt|Yozei|ru|Император Ёдзэй|sh|Car Yōzei|simple|Emperor Yōzei|sl|Cesar Jōzei|sv|Yozei|sw|Yozei wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิโยเซ|tl|Emperador Yōzei|tr|Yōzei|uk|Імператор Йодзей|ur|شہنشاہ یوزی|vi|Thiên hoàng Yōzei|yo|Emperor Yōzei|zh|陽成天皇|zh_min_nan|Yôzei Thian-hông|qid=Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation.
